column1: # Annotations that produced no name, and why. NAMED is DERIVED from the
# annot: tokens in the proposal tables and the names the tree defines --
# do not duplicate it here. A verdict and a citation are mutually exclusive;
# annotation_queue.py --check fails on an id carrying both.

# yields no rename), HELD (settled_by required), REJECTED (cannot support a name)

column6: names STORM_PARTICLE's subject from a witness that never read the tree; ../storm-particles/ earned the name as the intersection of amiga's ambient drift and msdos's particle tumble, and the family F00..F04 is already complete in both ports (INTRO.asm:376-380, drawn one per iteration at x=[0x07], y=[0x09] at 1145-1153)

measured: these are NOT members of CINEMATIC_PRISON_GREEN_TRACER_F0..F7 (0x864A..0x86B2, all eight drawn by one routine at PRISON.asm:2501-2515). They sit elsewhere in the bank (0x854A..0x8622) and are drawn by separate three-frame burst routines installed on their own channels -- DRAW_CIN_154_TO_156_3F_AT_A74B7DB1 on 0x38, DRAW_CIN_151_TO_153_3F_AT_40D20636 on 0x39 -- each opening with play id=0x0058 at a different freq/vol, all anchored x=160, y=[0x19]. So the subject the person gives (a sparkle of the lift) agrees with the tree's own neighbouring word, but the INDEX does not follow: three bursts of three, and F0..F7 already taken by the other family.
column7: what picks between the burst routines, and what [0x19] holds -- notes/dispatch-ladders/ for the first, and the y variable's writers for the second. Until then the family bounds are unknown and an index would be invented.

Person and tree disagree about the same constant, and #0120 says not to pick between earned names. The disagreement is itself the finding: the same session calls the figure at that anchor Buddy from frame 3073 on, after the cage falls, and the two sets sit in separate regions of the bytecode -- PRISON.asm:8849-10045 against 3631-3757. So the anchor is a slot and the scene decides who is in it.

column6: CV_FIGURE_WALK_RIGHT_UPPER_POSE_06 already carried this name when the annotation arrived, and the sentence agrees with it from a witness who had not read the tree: 'full right arm completely pointing downwards while the guard walks to the right'. UPPER_POSE is the layer, 06 the phase, RIGHT the direction -- all three confirmed independently by someone describing the picture. No rename: the name is already what the evidence supports, and the guard reading is not admissible as an actor word from this anchor (../actor-anchors/).

CINEMATIC_PRISON_BAR_PANEL_F0..F4 sit at the FIXED screen box x[109,125] y[22.5,41] in every frame, 16.0x18.0 throughout, and only the leaf count moves: 8, 7, 6, 5, 2. Channel 0x08 runs the family forwards then backwards -- DRAW_CIN_628_TO_625_4F before the undressing and DRAW_CIN_624_TO_628_5F after it -- so a fixed frame gains detail and then loses it. That is compatible with BOTH readings and discriminates neither. The committed name came from a render: '16.0x18.0, 8 paths, the most: a frame with its full set of vertical bars'. The person, also looking but in motion and in context, says 'the box inside which the guard's cloak is stored'. Two lookings that disagree, and this project's own rule is that two lookings agreeing is not evidence -- so two disagreeing establishes nothing either way.
column7: something non-visual that separates a barred frame from a container: whether anything is ever drawn INSIDE the box x[109,125] y[22.5,41] by another routine, and whether the 8-to-2 leaf progression removes parallel strokes (bars) or nested outlines (a lid over contents). notes/render-and-name/compose_run.py --progressive over DRAW_CIN_624_TO_628_5F_AT_499AFE0A would show which, and notes/scene-reading/composed_of.py can say whether any other constant lands in that box.
